headline: Preparing for Kitchen Cabinet Removal
articleBody:
Getting ready to remove kitchen cabinets might seem like a simple task, but a little prep work goes a long way in preventing headaches and damage. Whether you're planning a full renovation or just replacing old units, a solid plan makes the process much smoother.

First, you'll want to completely empty all your cabinets. It sounds obvious, but you'd be surprised how many forgotten items lurk in the back! As you empty them, it's a great time to sort and label the contents. Decide what you'll keep, what can be donated, and what's truly trash. If you're storing items during a remodel, clear, labeled bins can be a lifesaver when it's time to put everything back.

Next, make sure any adjacent appliances or utilities are either disconnected or thoroughly protected. If cabinets are near the sink, stove, or fridge, you might need to temporarily move those items or at least cover them well to prevent dust and debris. If there are any electrical outlets or switches within the cabinets, ensure the power to those circuits is turned off at your breaker box for safety. Similarly, if there's any plumbing (like for a sink or dishwasher) that runs through or behind cabinets you're removing, make sure the water supply is shut off.

Finally, plan for the disposal or reuse of the cabinets themselves. Are they in good enough shape to donate? Many charities will accept gently used cabinets. Or will they simply be discarded as construction waste? Knowing this beforehand will help you arrange for a dumpster or a pickup service. This preparation stage is crucial for a smooth and safe cabinet removal process, whether you're doing it yourself or bringing in pros like HH Remodeling LLC.
